No exact four-component match emerged; novelty remains unestablished. [HGN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.09217) combines long-/short-term preferences, feature/instance gates and item–item products, without a text branch or SASRec residual. [TLSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04760) combines global/local self-attention with time-lag-sensitive gating. [UniSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.05941) uses description embeddings, whitening and adaptors for transferable sequential representations. These establish substantial component-level precedent, but not the precise proposed combination.

A TF–IDF recurrence branch built exclusively from training prefixes offers inexpensive lexical interest accumulation; its distinctive contribution would require evidence beyond combining familiar components. If “training-only” means removing the branch at inference, it must transfer information through an auxiliary loss or distillation; it cannot directly supply inference scores. Useful simpler controls: normalized exponentially decayed ID-embedding pooling, long-/short-window mean pooling, and history-aware transitions. [HAM](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10034966/) combines general preferences with pooled recent associations and reports accuracy/runtime advantages over neural baselines in its experiments. [Fossil](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) combines history-based factored item similarity with personalized higher-order Markov transitions, directly testing whether sustained interests need textual recurrence.

Shortcut concerns remain hypotheses for this benchmark. IDF downweights common tokens but cannot guarantee removal of boilerplate or popularity proxies. [TASTE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14029) reports reduced popularity bias from text matching, so text is not inherently a popularity shortcut. [Sceptre](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.08839) distinguishes substitutes from complements, supporting the concern that similarity alone misses purchase context; its richer inputs are unavailable here. Compare generic-token removal, shuffled text, popularity-only scores and duplicate-title filtering as training/validation ablations. Keep the pinned evaluator: [sampled-metric research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) shows sampled rankings need not preserve full-catalog model ordering.
